summary: Chüan-ying Yen works in Buddhist studies, sinology, and history and archaeology. She earned her PhD from Harvard University, studying under doctoral supervisor John M. Rosenfield, tutor Chu-tsing Li, and teacher John Hay.

Chün-fang Yü works in Buddhist studies, sinology, and religious studies. She studied at Columbia University (~1964–1973) and under Nanting and Sheng Yen. She held posts at Rutgers University (~1972–2001) and Columbia University (~2001–2018; Emerita ~2018).

Claes Wennerberg (1939–1996) specialized in Indology and linguistics. He earned his PhD at the University of Gothenburg under Gösta Liebert (~1965–1981) and later served there as Docent and half-time Universitetslektor (~1982–1996).

Claire Chang works in Buddhist studies and psychology, having studied at the University of Sydney, Naropa University, and Nan Tien Institute. Her career includes positions at One Door Mental Health, UC Boulder, and Naropa University (2015–2019).

Clara Sue Kidwell (1941–2025) studied history and archaeology at the University of Oklahoma (PhD ~1966–1970). She held posts at UC Berkeley, the National Museum of the American Indian, University of Oklahoma, and UNC Chapel Hill (~2007–2011).

Clare Carlisle is a scholar of philosophy and religious studies who studied at Trinity College, Cambridge (1995–2002). She served as Lecturer in Philosophy at the University of Liverpool (~2006–2011) and became a professor at King's College London (~2020).

Clarence Herbert Hamilton (1886–1986) worked in Buddhist studies and philosophy, earning his PhD from the University of Chicago and studying at Union Theological Seminary. He held professorships at Hartford Seminary (1928–1931) and Oberlin College (1931–1952).

Clarence Linton Meader (1867–1967) was an Indology and linguistics scholar. He studied at the University of Michigan, Athens, Bonn, Munich, and Rome, and served as an Instructor in Latin at the University of Michigan (1893–1938).

Claude Charles Fauriel (1772–1844) was a French scholar of Indology and linguistics who studied under Alexander Hamilton and Antoine-Léonard Chézy. He co-founded the Société Asiatique and was Professor of Foreign Literature at the Sorbonne from 1830.

Claude Hagège is a linguist who studied under André Martinet and at institutions including the École Normale Supérieure. He held posts at the CNRS (~1965–1970), University of Poitiers (1970–1987), and Collège de France (1988–2006).

Claude Jacques (1929–2018) specialized in Indology and history and archaeology, studying under Armand Minard and George Cœdès. He served as director of the École française d'Extrême-Orient (~1965–1973) and taught at the EPHE (~1970–2001).

Claude Lévi-Strauss (1908–2009) was a philosopher and anthropologist who studied under Marcel Mauss. He held posts at the University of São Paulo (~1935–1939), the EPHE (~1950–1974), and the Collège de France as chair of Social Anthropology (1959–1982).

Claude-Auguste Court (1793–1880) was an Indology and archaeology figure who studied at École Polytechnique and École Spéciale Militaire de Saint-Cyr. He served in the Court of Ranjit Singh and the Sikh Khalsa Army as Engineer Officer (~1827–1843).

Claudia Benthien is a scholar of linguistics and related fields. She studied at Washington University and Humboldt University of Berlin, where she was an assistant professor (2000–2005) before becoming a Full Professor at the University of Hamburg in 2005.

Claudia Dellacasa works in Buddhist studies and related fields. She studied at Sapienza University of Rome and Durham University (PhD 2017–2021), later holding posts at Tübingen, Augsburg, University College Dublin (2022–2024), and the University of Glasgow (Lecturer 2024).
Claudia Weber is a scholar in Indology and religious studies who studied under teacher Hans-Joachim Klimkeit and project supervisor Gregor Ahn.

Claudie Marcel-Dubois (1913–1989) worked in Indology and ethnomusicology, studying under Marcel Mauss and Paul Masson-Oursel. She held posts at the Musée National des Arts et Traditions Populaires (1937–1981) and École Pratique des Hautes Études (from 1961).

Claudio Giacomino (1848–1923) was an Italian scholar in linguistics and Indology. He held teaching posts at Liceo Chiabrera-Martini and served as Professor ord. of Latin and Greek literature at Liceo Classico Massimo d'Azeglio.

Claudius Buchanan (1766–1815) worked in Indology and religious studies. Educated at the University of Glasgow and Queens' College, Cambridge, he served as a Church Mission Society missionary (1797–1808) and as Vice-Provost of Fort William College from 1799.

Claus Haebler (1931–2023) was a scholar of Indology and linguistics who studied under Friedrich Weller (~1949–1954) and Paul Thieme (~1954–1957). He held an academic post at the University of Münster (~1972–1996).
